goals: Mechanistic: quantify how initial water-table depth controls the fraction of a surface infiltration pulse that reaches the water table (recharge) vs is retained/lost in the unsaturated zone
key_processes: soil-moisture storage and retention above the water table
water-table rise (ZWT) response to a pulse

model_choice.rationale: 1-D vertical infiltration-to-water-table transport in a single column is exactly ELM's single-column strength; the question is idealized and needs a controlled WTD ladder, not spatial heterogeneity.

answerable: WTD control on pulse-to-water-table fraction across the shallow-to-intermediate range (0.5 m to ~28.8 m), given warm-start + spin-up
Monotonic attenuation/delay of recharge signal as initial WTD deepens within the aquifer range

not_answerable.aspect: WTD levels deeper than ~28.8 m, including the requested 50 m
not_answerable.why: ELM's aquifer range is clamped to 0.05-28.8 m; deeper targets pin the aquifer empty and become indistinguishable, so 30/40/50 m are not represented as distinct water tables

sampling_strategy.approach: controlled / not spatial — log-spaced factor ladder on initial WTD, all else fixed

bands: 50 m (REQUESTED — INFEASIBLE, records aquifer-empty pin only)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 7 answerable log-spaced WTD levels resolve the expected strong non-linearity (sharp drop in pulse fraction as the unsaturated column lengthens) across ELM's representable range 0.5-28.8 m; the 50 m level is documented but not counted as answerable due to the aquifer clamp. Log spacing over linear because attenuation scales with unsaturated-column length, not linearly.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: controlled / not spatial — one representative soil column and one representative forcing period held fixed across all levels; only the warm-start initial water table is varied.
sampling_strategy.replication: None across WTD levels (deterministic single-column). Optional paired no-pulse control run per level to isolate the pulse contribution to recharge.

sampling_plan.reason: Short vadose path — expect near-complete, rapid pulse transmission to the water table; anchors the high-fraction end of the response curve.
Transition zone where retention begins to noticeably attenuate and delay the pulse; resolves the curve's steepest region.
Long vadose path — expect strong attenuation and long delay, small fraction reaching WT within the window.
Deepest representable water table; low-fraction endpoint and boundary of what the aquifer can represent before the clamp.
Beyond ELM's 28.8 m aquifer clamp — logged as a not-answerable target, not an executable run.

validation_design.target_variable: fraction of infiltration pulse reaching the water table (ΔQRECHARGE / ΔZWT rise / aquifer-storage change vs no-pulse control)
validation_design.observation_source: physical expectation / literature (idealized experiment — no observations in brief)
validation_design.comparison: analog — qualitative check that the modeled response is monotonic in WTD (deeper -> smaller, more delayed pulse fraction) and consistent with vadose-zone theory; not co-located data validation
validation_design.metric: shape/monotonicity of pulse-fraction vs WTD curve; timing (lag-to-peak recharge) vs WTD

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: single representative soil + fixed representative forcing period; imposed infiltration pulse; initial water table set per-level via WTD-informed warm start; short spin-up to equilibrate the unsaturated profile before the pulse

requires_capabilities.capability: WTD-informed warm start with prescribed initial water-table depth per column
requires_capabilities.why: the factor being varied IS the initial water table; each level must be set to a specific WTD rather than the default ~8.8 m cold start
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire experiment — without it every level starts at the same WTD and the factor cannot be varied

requires_capabilities.capability: spin-up years to equilibrate the unsaturated profile before the pulse
requires_capabilities.why: recharge/ZWT read as initialization artifacts without spin-up; the pulse response must be measured against an equilibrated baseline
requires_capabilities.blocks: meaningful measurement of the pulse-to-water-table fraction

requires_capabilities.capability: prescribed / controllable surface infiltration pulse of known magnitude and timing
requires_capabilities.why: the experiment applies a defined pulse and tracks its fate; needs a repeatable forcing event identical across all levels
requires_capabilities.blocks: clean attribution of recharge change to the pulse

requires_capabilities.capability: recharge / water-table flux diagnostics (QRECHARGE, ZWT, aquifer storage) in history output at sub-daily-to-daily resolution
requires_capabilities.why: the target metric is the fraction and timing of pulse water arriving at the WT

requires_capabilities.capability: deep-aquifer / extended vadose representation below 28.8 m
requires_capabilities.why: requested range extends to 50 m but ELM clamps the aquifer at 28.8 m
requires_capabilities.blocks: the deep half of the requested WTD range (30-50 m)

assumptions: A single representative soil texture is acceptable for isolating the WTD effect; soil is held fixed so any response difference is attributable to initial WTD, not texture.
One representative forcing period plus a prescribed pulse is sufficient; inter-annual climate variability is deliberately excluded to keep the experiment controlled.
Fraction 'reaching the water table' is operationalized as pulse-attributable change in recharge/aquifer storage within a fixed post-pulse window, measured against a paired no-pulse control.
Vegetation/root-zone parameters are held fixed and default; root-zone soil moisture is a fast state left at model default under warm start.
Log-spaced WTD levels (0.5-28.8 m) adequately capture the expected non-linear attenuation; finer levels can be added if the curve is under-resolved.
open_questions: What pulse magnitude and duration should be imposed (e.g. a single large storm vs a multi-day event)? This sets whether shallow WTs saturate/pond.
Which representative soil texture (sand/loam/clay) — or should texture be a second controlled factor since it strongly co-controls vadose travel time?
What post-pulse observation window defines 'reaches the water table' (days vs a full season)? Deep WTs may need a long window to register any arrival.
Is a ParFlow/Fan-style deep prior desired later to push initial WTD beyond 28.8 m and recover the requested 50 m level?
